title: YouTube Comments: `imageUrl` Now Output-Only
summary: The `imageUrl` property in `CommentSnippet` is now read-only, meaning developers can no longer set it. Additionally, several media upload endpoints now accept a broader range of content types.
details:
A significant breaking change has been introduced: the `imageUrl` property within the `CommentSnippet` schema is now explicitly `readOnly`. This means any attempts to provide or modify an image URL when creating or updating comments will fail. The API will now only return this property if a comment contains an image or GIF, served as a signed link with a six-hour TTL. Developers must update their applications to reflect this change.

Separately, various media upload methods across the API have seen updates to their accepted MIME types. Methods like `captions.insert`, `channelBanners.insert`, `playlistImages.insert`, `thumbnails.set`, `videos.insert`, and `watermarks.set` now generally offer more flexibility in the `Content-Type` headers they accept, often including `application/octet-stream` or a broader `*/*`.
